name: Okta tenant OpenID configuration (public, unauthenticated well-known document)
tier_rationale: Established company with published terms, a privacy policy and a business offering (A8 trusted); P371 provider_tier 'trusted' (council #1).

reliability.justification: First-party answer of Okta's own tenant host: a 200 OpenID document whose issuer is the requested <name>.okta.com proves the tenant exists. It never proves which organisation owns the tenant (homonyms): a candidate until corroborated (P371 FC5).

openid_configuration.title: Okta tenant discovery: https://<name>.okta.com/.well-known/openid-configuration (200 + issuer = tenant exists, 403 E0000006 = no tenant)
openid_configuration.notes: Research C0797, live 2026-11-26 (batch p3-G13-1): okta.okta.com answered 200 JSON with issuer https://okta.okta.com and cache-control max-age=86400; a random name answered 403 JSON errorCode E0000006 (the documented absence marker, read raw: never through get_json). /.well-known/okta-organization answers 200 for ANY name and is never built (P371 FC2). Login, authn, authorize, token, user and factor endpoints are never requested (rule 2, P371 FC3). Politeness budget (not published by Okta for this document): 0.5 request/s and 60 per day per egress, one GET per candidate, no retries.

notes: Owned by batch p3-G13-1 (P371, module saas_tenant_discovery). Only the fixed FC2 path is ever built: the candidate name is the only value Okta receives (a normalised organisation label from the org profile or an authorized scope file, never a username or e-mail). Cookies are never stored or replayed by the core client.
